finding.claim: /checkout computes the charge total from client-supplied price and qty. An attacker can set price to a tiny or negative value, or qty to a negative number, so the total is near zero or negative. The user is then charged that amount (or credited) for the items.
finding.source: req.body.items[].price and req.body.items[].qty (authenticated user's JSON body)

trace.note: total = sum(i.price * i.qty) using values taken directly from the request body; no catalog lookup, no validation
the unvalidated total is passed to payments.charge
the total is echoed back as the amount charged

finding.guards_checked: No server-side price lookup, no check that qty is positive or an integer, and no check that total > 0 on this route. The sibling /checkout-v2 route (cart.js:13-14) shows the intended pattern: catalog price plus clamped qty. The older /checkout route is still mounted and reachable. No middleware is visible in this file, and the only file in the directory is cart.js.

verdict.reason: cart.js:5 sums client-supplied i.price * i.qty with no catalog lookup or validation, and cart.js:6 passes that total to req.payments.charge, whereas /checkout-v2 (cart.js:13-14) uses catalog prices and a clamped qty. An authenticated user could therefore reduce or negate the charge. Auth middleware and the payments implementation are not in the directory, so only the route code was checked.
